tool_input.args: Increase organic traffic for this SaaS. Live site: http://127.0.0.1:45087. Source repo: current working directory. GSC export available in ./gsc/. Please run a full analysis using the live GSC export data plus a technical/content audit of the site, then produce a prioritized action plan and implement the highest-impact fixes directly in the repo.

result:
Build verified clean and the site now serves correctly. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed:

**The core problem:** this SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (an email-cleanup tool) to "Lumina" (an AI meeting assistant), but the migration was left half-done in the repo. GSC confirms the damage: every one of the 40 tracked queries and most indexed pages are leftover email/inbox-cleanup terms pulling thousands of impressions at page-4-5 positions with near-zero clicks — and there isn't a single query related to "meeting notes" or "AI meeting assistant." The actual current business has zero organic visibility.

Fixes applied:
- **`app/layout.tsx`** — the `<title>`/description were still "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" while the homepage content was all about Lumina/meeting notes. Fixed to match the real product, added canonical URL, OG/Twitter cards, and `Organization`/`SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD.
- **`/features` and `/pricing`** — linked from nav but didn't exist in the repo (404). Built real pages with proper per-page metadata.
- **`/faq`** — redirected to `/#faq` but that anchor didn't exist anywhere. Added an actual FAQ section with `FAQPage` schema to the homepage.
- **Blog** — the index page was client-rendered, fetching from `/api/posts`, which doesn't exist — Googlebot would see "Loading posts…" forever, and the sitemap never included any post URLs. Converted to a server-rendered index + `/blog/[slug]` routes with `generateStaticParams`, per-post metadata, and `BlogPosting` schema.
- **Content strategy** — the 12 already-indexed blog posts (confirmed via the live site) are all old InboxZap content ("How to Reach Inbox Zero," "Gmail Storage Full?," etc.) — completely off-brand for an AI meeting assistant. Wrote 6 new posts targeting real topics for the current product (meeting notes templates, transcription, action items, meeting overload, async standups, AI-assistant comparison) and 301-redirected the legacy `/blog/post-:id` URLs to the new `/blog` index instead of letting them 404 or stay indexed with the wrong product.
- **Sitemap** — now includes `/features`, `/pricing`, and every blog post, not just 4 static URLs.
- Added a real OG image so social/share previews aren't broken.

Ran `npm install && npm run build` and smoke-tested every route locally — build is clean, all redirects and new pages return correct status codes.

One unrelated thing worth flagging: `npm install` reported Next.js 14.2.5 has a known security advisory (patched in a later 14.2.x). I didn't touch dependencies since it's outside the SEO scope — let me know if you'd like me to bump it.
